text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 3.9% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of nearly 18%. The immediate trigger appears to be political uncertainty: yesterday's news that Democrats plan investigations into Trump administration energy deals and Venezuela intervention has created concern that policy shifts could disrupt the refining business. This comes on top of an earnings announcement earlier in the week, suggesting investors may be reassessing the company's outlook in a changing political environment.

The broader context makes the stock more vulnerable to this news. U.S. oil prices have weakened to under $100 a barrel while global prices sit at $107, narrowing the refining margin — the profit refineries make by processing crude into fuel. With refineries running at 94.5% capacity and gasoline and diesel inventories relatively high, there's less room for pricing power. Political risk layered onto tighter margins has made the stock less attractive to hold.
